title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In cote 140-3, Grothendieck works on the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the loop/braid-type relations that govern Galois and Teichmüller actions on profinite fundamental groups. This page is part of a long structural computation.

The objects:
- M is a group, apparently of automorphisms or outer-type data. M^? → M is a central-type extension with kernel μ_ρ (p. 626', (55)).
- L_{ρ0}, L_{σ0} are 'loop' subgroups attached to two points or cusps ρ0, σ0.
- N_{ρ0}, N_{σ0} are normalizers in M, and Z_{σ0} is a centralizer in M. The '!' versions are intersections with a subgroup M^!.
- Γ0 = Γ_{ρ0,σ0} is a common quotient.
- M^? is described on the previous page by (122) as a fibre product N^?_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0} Z^!_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M.
- The symbol written ♮ (on the next page apparently M^G, with M^G = G^G_{ρ,σ}) denotes a subgroup M^♮ ⊂ M, plausibly the invariants under a finite group G. The marginal note suggests it is related to an inner-automorphism group Int(M^♮) inside an orbifold-type fundamental group Π~_Ω.
- M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} (118) is the analogous fibre product of normalizers over Γ0 lying above M^♮.
- (124) defines M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} = M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} ∩ M^?, the intersection taken inside N_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0} N_{σ0} ×_{Γ0} M.

This page:
1. The induced map M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ is the restriction of M^? → M. Its kernel is therefore μ_ρ ∩ M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0}.
2. By construction (119), μ_ρ ⊂ M^♮_{ρ0,σ0}, hence μ_ρ ⊂ M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0}.
3. This gives the commutative diagram (126). Its bottom row is 1 → μ_ρ → M^? → M → 1. Its top row is 1 → μ_ρ → M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮, mapping to the bottom row by inclusions.
4. Grothendieck then asserts (**), to be proved in a lemma: M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ is an epimorphism, 'contrary to what one imagined'. So the top row is also a short exact sequence, and M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} is an extension of M^♮ by μ_ρ, i.e. the restriction of the extension M^? to M^♮.
5. Combining (118) and (122), the definition gives (127): M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} ≅ N^{♮?}_{ρ0} ×_{Γ0^♮} Z^{♮!}_{σ0} ×_{Γ0^♮} M^♮. Here (128) gives N^{♮?}_{ρ0} = N^?_{ρ0} ∩ N^♮_{ρ0} = N^?_{ρ0} ∩ M^♮, and Z^{♮!}_{σ0} = Z^!_{σ0} ∩ N^♮_{σ0} = Z^!_{σ0} ∩ M^♮.
6. On the next page, surjectivity is reduced to the surjectivity of the two projections N^{♮?}_{ρ0} → Γ0^♮ and Z^{♮!}_{σ0} → Γ0^♮. A lifting argument is begun via conditions a)–d) of (107). It is then explicitly abandoned: 'j'ai omis les vérifications… ce n'est pas urgent'. Grothendieck turns instead to the 'tame' and 'formalisés' special cases.

Purpose. The aim is to show that the extension M^? of M by μ_ρ (a group of roots of unity or cyclotomic-type kernel) restricts well to the ♮-substructure, compatibly with the normalizer/centralizer fibre-product description. This is a step in determining the structure of the groups M_{ρ,σ} that occur in the loop equations.
errors: The top row of (126) is written as exact only on the left; exactness on the right is exactly the claim (**), which is not proved here or on the next page (verifications explicitly omitted).
The sentence 'et donc, contrairement à ce qu'on imaginait' is left unfinished.
In the body text the source of the map is written M^?_{ρ0,σ0}, whereas by (124) it should be M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0}. This is a notational slip, partly a transcription issue.

(127) presupposes that the intersection (124) is compatible with both fibre-product decompositions. This needs Γ0^♮ to be the image of M^♮ in Γ0 and the two projections to be compatible, which is not checked.

ideas.what: Kernel of a restricted map lies in the kernel μ_ρ of the ambient extension, giving a morphism of short exact sequences (126).
ideas.modern_name: restriction/pullback of a group extension to a subgroup

ideas.what: Description of the restricted extension as a triple fibre product of normalizer/centralizer intersections over a common quotient Γ0^♮ (127)–(128).
ideas.modern_name: fibre-product description of stabilizers of a pair of cusp/loop subgroups (Teichmüller-type groupoid computations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific attribution; related in spirit to Galois–Teichmüller/GT work (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak)

ideas.what: Claim (**): the ♮-part of the extension still surjects onto M^♮ ('contrary to what one imagined'), reduced on the next page to surjectivity of two normalizer projections onto Γ0^♮.
ideas.modern_name: surjectivity of a restricted central extension; lifting of fixed points/invariants

missed.claim: The surjectivity M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ is asserted, and Grothendieck notes it reverses his earlier expectation. The proof is only sketched and then explicitly abandoned. It reduces to showing that N^{♮?}_{ρ0} → Γ0^♮ and Z^{♮!}_{σ0} → Γ0^♮ are onto.
missed.quote: M^?_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ est un épimorphisme, et donc, contrairement à ce qu'on imaginait
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor open verification inside an unpublished structural analysis of loop-equation groups M_{ρ,σ}. It would matter only to someone reconstructing Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The objects are too implicitly defined on this page for it to be a recognizable open problem for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine diagram chase in a long technical computation. It contains one asserted but unproved surjectivity, flagged as unexpected by Grothendieck himself. There is no new concept or connection recognizable from this page alone.
transcription_corrections: The source of the map in the first lines and in (**) should read M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} (as in the inclusion M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} ⊃ M^{♮?}_{ρ0,σ0} drawn in diagram (126)), not M^?_{ρ0,σ0}.
The ♮ symbol appears to be the same superscript the next page transcribes as G (M^G); it is likely a G-like superscript, not a musical natural sign.
(127): the fibre-product subscripts are Γ0^♮ (crossed-out attempts beneath); the middle factor is Z^{♮!}_{σ0} (a Z overwritten on a crossed-out letter), not ℤ.

(128) first line: N^{♮?}_{ρ0} = N^?_{ρ0} ∩ N^♮_{ρ0} = N^?_{ρ0} ∩ M^♮ (the image looks like N^?; the transcription's N^! is likely wrong). Second line: Z^{♮!}_{σ0} = Z^!_{σ0} ∩ N^♮_{σ0} = Z^!_{σ0} ∩ M^♮.
